transcript: Yesterday, I saw Adam Driver in Hold On To Me Darling at the Lucille Hotel Theatre in the West Village. Written by Kenneth Lonergan, whose other work I've loved such as The Waverly Gallery and Manchester By The Sea, this play is about a country star in a life crisis after his mother dies. He resents how fame has trapped him and he's looking for something real. Now, this is a comedy with some serious moments, but I found it mostly humorous in a sort of tragic way. All of the characters are a little lost in one way or another and a lot of the comedy comes from the characters’ awkwardness or them just saying really peculiar things. Adam Driver is excellent. His character is explosive and impulsive, and I imagine he must be exhausted by performing this role, but he seems to do it with ease. Much like the direction, his performance is very natural and the character felt believable to me. As far as critiques though, this was too long. At three hours, I felt the first 70% of it was well paced but it lost steam toward the end, and unfortunately it didn't end with closure in a way that I felt could have justified the run time. I guess if I could rate the first 70% of the show by itself, solid 4 out of 5 stars. And even with the strengths of this production, the tickets are simply way too expensive, especially given the sightlines in this theater are kind of terrible. My seat was a hundred bucks, which at this point is considered a steal, believe it or not, but anything above that price I think is a stretch. Unless you're a die hard Adam Driver fan, this is not a must see. But nevertheless, glad I got to experience it without completely breaking the bank. With that, another playbill for my collection.
